items.question: What is the sign of notchCalculator(previous, current).notches? Clarification C5, which the document skips, presumably defined it. Settled: notchChange is a signed integer (positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged); direction is exactly 'downgrade' | 'upgrade' | 'unchanged'; wl is 0|1|2; the returned object has exactly the keys notches, direction, wl. NOT settled: whether notches is signed like notchChange or an unsigned magnitude with direction carrying the sign. For downgrades both agree (BBB+ -> BB+: 3); for upgrades they differ (BB+ -> BBB+: -3 or 3).
options: A: notches is signed and identical to notchChange: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0. BB+ -> BBB+ gives { notches: -3, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }.
B: notches is the unsigned magnitude |notchChange| (0..18); the sign lives only in direction. BB+ -> BBB+ gives { notches: 3, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }.
items.impact: Changes the public contract other POC parts import 'exactly'. Consumers that render or compare notches break if they assume the other convention. Upgrade ACs and test data cannot be written until decided. Downgrade and unchanged cases are identical under A and B.

items.answer: notchCalculator(...).notches is signed exactly like notchChange: downgrade positive, upgrade negative (BB → BBB is -3); direction says the same in words.

notchChange, notchCalculator and countryRatingChangeWl validate both arguments. A value is accepted when, after trim() and case-insensitive matching, it equals one of the 19 C1 ratings. Anything else throws RangeError with no fallback: '', whitespace-only, unknown grades ('D', 'NR', 'Baa1'), inner-space 'BBB +', Unicode minus 'BBB−', and non-strings (null, undefined, 3, {}). countryRatingChangeWl inherits this via notchChange. Message text is not contract (X-error-message).
Nothing exists to stay compatible with (src/ and test/ hold only .gitkeep; single seed commit). The new names and semantics are binding from day one. No versioning (private package 0.1.0).

items.answer: Nothing is stored; ratings come in as arguments.
No external system is called; the public rating source is out of scope.
Synchronous only; all exports are deterministic and none returns a Promise. No queues, events or jobs.
No latency/volume target is set; constant-time lookups on a 19-entry scale.
In-process pure functions with no runtime dependency; nothing to degrade.
Only input validation applies: both arguments must be on the C1 scale after trim and case-folding, else RangeError. No authentication, authorisation or secrets: no endpoint, no I/O.
Inputs are only rating grade strings; no client identity or personal data enters, is logged or stored.
No audit trail in this slice; an analyst's edit is just a different input.
No logging, metrics or tracing: pure functions, no printed output.
POC slice; the only domain rules are the business-confirmed scale and WL thresholds; no regulation or model-risk constraint is named.

Dev unit tests (node:test + node:assert/strict) in test/ratings/notch.test.mjs and test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs; QA integration tests through the public exports in separate files under test/integration/. Test data: the 19 ratings as given, lower-cased and padded; C2 examples; C6; C3; extremes AAA->CCC- (+18) and CCC-->AAA (-18); the RangeError inputs of CON-errors. No coverage percentage is set. unchanged must yield +0, not -0 (Object.is).
